chunks: Al-Hakim Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sawli narrated to us, Oun ibn Muhammad al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Abul Husayn Muhammad ibn Abi Ibad narrated to me, and he was known for listening (to music) and drinking nabidh, saying:
I asked Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) about listening (to music), and he said: 'The people of Hijaz have an opinion regarding it, but it is within the realm of falsehood and amusement.'
Have you not heard God, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: 'And when they pass by vain talk, they pass by it with honor.'

key_terms.السَّمَاعِ: Listening (specifically to music or vocal recitation)
key_terms.اللَّهْوِ: Amusement/distraction (often paired with falsehood to denote non-serious or vain activities)
key_terms.النَّبِيذِ: Nabidh (a type of fermented drink, often used as a generic term for wine/intoxicants in fiqh)
key_terms.الْحِجَازِ: Hijaz (a region in western Arabia, often representing the scholarly consensus or specific juristic view of that area)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on listening to music according to Imam Ar-Ridha (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Imam Ar-Ridha (a.s.) clarifies that while the people of Hijaz may hold varying opinions on listening to music, it fundamentally belongs to the realm of *batil* (falsehood) and *lahw* (amusement/distraction). He substantiates this by citing Surah Al-Mu’minun, verse 72, which commands believers to pass by vain talk with dignity, thereby linking auditory entertainment to the broader concept of avoiding spiritual distraction.
